sub: Two people who just met. Small talk → real.

1.name: Perception
q: What made you say yes to tonight?~Guess my reason first. Get it right and I owe you a second, more honest one.
What's your honest first impression of me?
Guess one thing about me — I'll tell you if you're right.
Guess something I'm weirdly good at that never comes up. Two guesses.~Then I tell you, and you tell me yours.
Were you the same kid you are now, or a totally different person?
On three, both say the last thing that genuinely made you laugh out loud.~Whoever's is funnier picks who answers first next.
If we skipped the small talk, what should I actually ask you?
Name a small thing that instantly makes you like someone.~Then tell me whether I've done it tonight. Don't be polite about it.
Guess my most-used app. One shot.~Wrong, and I get to look at your screen time.
Both point: which of us leaves a text unanswered for three days? Three, two, one.~Pointed at yourself? Explain.
What could you talk about for an hour without getting bored?
Guess what I wanted to be when I was ten.~Then say whether you can still see it in me.
Guess the best compliment I've ever been given.~Then give me a better one, if you can.
Where do you feel most like yourself?
Five seconds, no thinking: what tiny thing ruins my day embarrassingly fast? Go.~Then I tell you the real one.
Mountains or the sea. Pick one and commit — 'depends' isn't an answer.~Now I argue you chose wrong.
What's the story you always end up telling at dinners?
Guess what people assume about me that's just wrong.~This is a test of how well you've been listening.
What's your relationship with mornings?
Say three words you'd use for me based on tonight alone. Out loud.~Then I tell you the three my friends actually use.
Pick the song that sets the mood for a night like this. Play ten seconds of it.~I rate the choice out of ten and have to justify the score.
What's the last thing that made you go 'I have to tell someone'?
Guess what I'm a little too competitive about.~Then we find out by competing at it, right now, badly.
On three, both say your 1am comfort order.~Whoever's is worse has to defend it.
What's the most spontaneous thing you've done lately?
Do first impressions stick for you, or do people surprise you?~Then tell me exactly what I'd have to do tonight to change yours.
What's something you've changed your mind about recently?
Guess the red flag I find weirdly attractive.~If you guess it and it's you, say so.
Describe your perfect Sunday.
What are you quietly hoping I'm like?~Say it before I answer. No adjusting once you've heard mine.
Guess the last thing I Googled before I left the house tonight.~Then I show you. No scrolling past anything.
If your dating profile was one honest sentence, what would it say?
Do your go-to opening line on me right now, properly, like we've never met.~I rate it out of ten and tell you whether it would have worked.
Guess my star sign — then tell me if you even believe in that stuff.
Guess the most 'you' thing in my bag or pockets.~Then we both empty them and find out.
Cats or dogs, and what does that say about you?
Name a ridiculous hill you'll die on.~Defend it for thirty seconds while I try to talk you off it.
What would your group chat call this date if they were watching live?
Tell me your worst first-date story.~Then I rate tonight against it, out of ten, out loud.
What show will you defend even though you know it's bad?
Guess my tell for when I'm actually into someone.~Then tell me whether you've seen it tonight.
Hand me your phone and open the camera roll. I pick a photo, you tell me the story behind it.
What trend were you way too late to catch onto?
Order for me — whatever you think I'd want.~I'll tell you how close you got, and what it says that you guessed that.
What's the most impulsive thing sitting in your online cart right now?
On three, both say your 'ick'.~If either of us has done the other's tonight, own up now.
Sunrise or sunset person, and when did you last actually catch one?
Give yourself a compliment nobody's said yet.~Then I say whether I'd have got there on my own.
What's the emoji you use way too often?
What's a rule you break on purpose and don't feel bad about?
Guess my villain origin story.~Then tell me yours, and make it worse than mine.
What's the last thing you did that would shock your younger self?
If we swapped playlists right now, which song would give you away first?
Name your toxic trait. Then I guess how many times it's shown up tonight — a number.~You confirm or deny. No negotiating it down.
What's a purchase you've made that's extremely 'you'?
What's on your bucket list that you haven't told many people about?
What's your walk-out song, if you had one?
Beach holiday or city break. Pick fast, no hedging.~Now defend it against me for thirty seconds.
Say a hot take that would start a fight at dinner.~I disagree out loud, and neither of us backs down for a full minute.
What's the most 'main character energy' thing you've ever done?
Guess what I do for a living — closest guess gets the real answer.
What's your honest verdict on splitting the bill tonight?
Do you have a 'type', and how close am I to it?~A number out of ten is allowed, but only if you explain it.
What's the last white lie you told, and was it a good one?
Guess which outfit almost didn't make the cut tonight.~Then I tell you, and you rate the one I picked instead.
Are you the friend who plans the whole trip, or the one who shows up with a bag five minutes before?
Name a word you say too often. You're banned from it for the rest of the night.~Every slip, I get one free question.
What's a skill you wish you had that has nothing to do with your job?
What conspiracy theory do you secretly enjoy, even if you don't believe a word of it?
What's the most chaotic thing happening in one of your group chats right now?
What song are you embarrassed to admit you know every word to?
Both guess the other's phone battery. Numbers out loud, on three.~Closest one gets to ask anything.

2.name: Connection
q: What's a risk you're glad you didn't talk yourself out of?
Guess who had the biggest hand in making me who I am.~Then I tell you, and you say what made you guess that.
What are you working on about yourself right now?
On three, both say when you feel most alive.~If they're different kinds of answer, that's the conversation.
What's a moment that quietly changed the direction of your life?
What did you have to unlearn from how you grew up?~I'm not allowed to say anything until you've finished. Take the space.
Guess something I want that I don't say out loud very often.~Wrong is the good outcome here. Ask what it actually is.
More afraid of being alone, or of settling? Pick one — you don't get both.~Then defend it against the version of you that would pick the other.
What does a good life look like to you — not the highlight-reel version?
When did you last cry, and did it help?~Answer, then I tell you whether I'd have guessed that about you.
What version of yourself are you glad you outgrew?
Guess what I need more of right now — rest, people, money, or something to work toward.~Then I do the same for you. Neither of us gets to be offended.
What's the hardest thing you've been through that you're okay telling me?
What are you proud of that rarely comes up?
Who do you miss?~Say the name out loud. Then tell me one specific thing, not a summary.
What's a belief you hold that most people around you don't?
Guess when I feel lonely even around people.~Then I tell you, and you say whether you recognised it.
What's the kindest thing someone has done for you?
On three, both say what you're still trying to prove, and to whom.~Same moment. No hearing mine first.
What's something you've forgiven yourself for — or are trying to?
From what you've seen, what does real love actually look like?~Then I say whether I've seen it too, or whether I'm still guessing.
What part of yourself do you protect the most?
Guess the dream I've quietly put on a shelf.~Then name yours. Neither of us is allowed to say we don't have one.
What do you know you do when you're falling for someone?
Name the gap between who you are and who people think you are.~Then I tell you which version I've been talking to tonight.
What fear has been running quietly in the background lately?
When did you last feel truly understood?~Answer it, then I ask one follow-up. You don't get to pick the follow-up.
What would you do if you knew you couldn't fail — and what's stopping you now?
Guess what I wish someone would just know without me explaining it.~Then I tell you, and you decide whether that's fair of me.
What's something you have never once regretted saying yes to?
Name a pattern in your family you're consciously trying not to repeat.~Then say how you'd know if you were failing at it.
What does 'home' mean to you these days?
When did you last surprise yourself?
What do you need from someone before you can actually feel safe with them?~Then I say honestly whether I could do that.
Is there an apology you never got but still needed?
Say a value you'd never compromise on, even for the right person.~I get to test it with one hypothetical. You have to answer it.
What did success look like to you ten years ago — and what does it look like now?
Guess my love language — the honest one, not the quiz version.~Then I guess yours. Whoever's further off explains why they read it that way.
What are you fiercely loyal to?
Who believed in you before you believed in yourself?~Then say whether you've ever told them.
Does ambition drive you or exhaust you, if you're honest?
Guess something I've inherited from a parent, good or bad.~You've had an hour to work it out. Then I tell you.
When did you actually become an adult — not your 18th, the real moment?~On three, both answer. The younger age explains first.
What scares you about getting older?
What do you do when no one's watching that says the most about you?~Then I tell you what I'd have guessed, and you say which is worse.
What's your honest relationship with money, underneath the practical stuff?
What does 'enough' feel like to you?
Guess something I want that I'm almost scared to admit I want.~Then say yours. This is the card neither of us gets to skip cheaply.
When did you last choose yourself over what someone expected of you?
Who would you call at 3am, no explanation needed?~Then say whether they know they're that person.
Who or what have you lost that still shapes how you love people?
Name a pattern you keep repeating in relationships, even when you see it coming.~Then I ask whether it's started tonight. You answer straight.
Guess what I need to hear more often and never ask for.~Then I tell you — and if you were right, say it to me properly.
When did you last feel like the outsider in a room?
Does failure wreck you or teach you?
What's a story you used to tell about yourself that isn't true anymore?~Tell me the old version first, in the old voice. Then the real one.
What's still healing, even if most of it already has?
Guess what makes me feel chosen.~Then tell me yours, and I'll tell you whether I've done any of it tonight.
How honest can you actually be about needing people?
On three, both say what you're quietly building toward right now.~Then say what would have to happen for you to give it up.
What's something you believed as a kid that you're a little sad isn't true?
What does your inner critic sound like — whose voice is it, if you're honest?~Say a line it says, in its voice, out loud.
What's a boundary you had to learn to hold, and who taught you the hard way?
When have you been braver for someone else than you've ever been for yourself?~Then I ask why that's easier. You don't get to say 'it just is'.
What's a fear you've actually made peace with?
Guess a risk I talked myself out of that I still think about.~Then name yours, and say whether it's too late.
What does grief look like for you — fast and loud, or slow and quiet?
How do you take care of yourself on the days that are quietly hard?
What's advice you give often but struggle to take yourself?~Give it to me now, properly. Then I give it straight back.
What's something you're grateful for now that you resented at the time?
Say something you're quietly afraid people would think less of you for.~Then I say whether it changes anything. You take the answer either way.

3.name: Reflection
q: Guess what I've noticed about you tonight that surprised me.~Then I tell you. Unedited.
What's something you almost said earlier but held back?
On three, both say how you feel right now, in one word.~Then the one who played it safer goes again, properly.
Name one thing you already like about me.~I'm not allowed to deflect it, laugh, or say thanks for thirty seconds.
When did you feel closest to me tonight?
What are you curious about that you haven't asked me yet?~Ask it now. Out loud. I answer whatever it is.
Guess what I'm like when no one's watching.~Then I tell you how close that was, and it's the honest version.
Has anything about me shifted since your first impression?~Say the before and the after. Both out loud.
What would you regret not telling me before tonight ends?
Guess the question I'm hoping you'll ask me.~Get it right and you have to ask it. Get it wrong and I tell you what it was.
On three, both say what you think we have in common that isn't obvious.~Same answer? That's a real one. Different? Both make your case.
Do you feel like yourself around me right now?~A number out of ten, then the explanation. The number comes first.
What about tonight will you still remember next week?
Say the bravest thing you could say to me right now.~Then I rate the bravery out of ten. Under five and you go again.
If tonight is all we get, what do you want me to remember about you?
Guess what I'm protecting myself from with you.~Then I tell you, and I don't get to make it sound better than it is.
On three, both say what you hope happens after tonight.~You don't get to hear mine first. That's the whole point of this card.
What's something you want to thank me for?
If you're honest, where do you feel this going?~Answer, then I ask one follow-up and you answer it straight.
Say what you want more of from me, right now.~I have to give a real answer — yes, no, or not yet. 'Maybe' isn't allowed.
What's true for you that's hard to say out loud?
Guess what I needed to hear tonight.~If you're right, say it to me properly. If you're wrong, I tell you and you say it anyway.
How did I make you feel tonight?~Then I tell you whether that's what I was going for. Neither of us softens it.
What's the realest thing you can tell me before we call it?
What's one thing about this you don't want to forget?
On three, both say what you want to happen in the next five minutes.~Whatever comes out, it stands.
Gut reaction — yes or no to a second date. Don't think about it.~Both answer at the same time. No reading the room first.
Guess what I'm nervous to admit I'm already feeling.~Then I tell you, and you decide what to do with it.
Name a physical detail about me you've noticed and haven't said.~Say it plainly. I don't get to make a joke of it.
If tonight were a film, what would you cut?~Then I tell you the scene I'd keep, and we find out if it's the same one.
Tell the version of tonight you'll give your friends tomorrow — out loud, in that voice.~Then tell me the version you'll keep to yourself.
What does the silence between us feel like right now?
Do you trust your gut about this? What's it telling you?
Guess what I want you to ask me that you haven't yet.~Then ask it, whether you got it right or not.
Is anything making you hesitate right now?~Say it. I stay quiet until you're completely finished.
Five seconds: what would you say if you were braver than you're being? Go.~Now say it properly, with the time you didn't have.
Beginning or a nice one-off — pick one, and say which you're hoping for.~Both answer on three. No hedging, no 'we'll see'.
What would you change about how tonight started, if anything?
What's a promise you'd make if this turns into something?
What did tonight teach you about what you actually want?
Guess the question I'm hoping you don't ask me.~Right, and you have to ask it anyway. Wrong, and I tell you what it was.
What does chemistry feel like to you, physically, right now?
Do you believe in knowing early? Is this that?
What would you do if I told you right now that I like you?~Answer as though I just did. Because I might have.
What's a line you won't cross tonight, and why does it matter to you?
If you said yes to me tonight, what would you want it to mean?
Have you thought about kissing me tonight?~Yes or no, on three, both of us. Explanations come after, not before.
What are you proud of yourself for, in how you showed up tonight?
Say the bravest question you could ask me right now — then ask it.~I answer properly. No dodging, no turning it around.
What would you regret not doing before we say goodnight?
Guess my favourite moment from tonight.~Then I tell you mine, and you say whether you'd have picked it for me.
What's changed in how you're sitting or holding yourself since we first sat down?
Name a question I asked tonight that you answered less than completely honestly.~Answer it again. Properly, this time.
If I leaned in right now, what would you do?~Answer out loud. Nobody's leaning yet — that's what makes it answerable.
What's something you hope I don't compare you to — an ex, a type, anything?
Is there a version of you I haven't met yet — and when do I get to?
Guess the answer you're most afraid I'll give you tonight.~Then ask me the question it belongs to.
Nervous to completely comfortable — where are you, one to ten?~Both say a number on three. Then whichever moved most tonight explains why.
What does my laugh do to you, if anything?
Say what you want to be doing with your hands right now that you're not.~Then leave them exactly where they are. For now.
Guess the last thing I said that's still sitting with you.~Then I tell you mine, and we find out whether either of us was listening.

wild: Hold eye contact for ten seconds. No talking. Then say the first word that comes.
Show me the last photo you took — no cheating, no explaining first.
Trade a secret. Small is fine. You go first.
Describe me to a stranger in one sentence.
Play the song that matches this exact moment.
Give me a genuine compliment — the kind you'd usually keep to yourself.
Read me your last text and tell me the story behind it.
Guess my love language. Then tell me yours.
Swap phones and pick the other's next song. No previews.
Sit in silence together for fifteen seconds. Notice how it feels.
Tell me one thing you like about me, starting with 'I noticed…'
Say something you'd only say a few drinks from now.
Rate tonight out of ten — and say what would make it a ten.
Tell me the thought you almost didn't share.
Take a photo of me right now, exactly as I look. Keep it.
Finish this out loud: 'What I'm not saying is…'
Do an impression of the other person's laugh.
Show them your camera roll's most-used folder or album — no explaining first.
Text one friend right now: 'rate this date so far.' Read the reply out loud.
Order for each other off the menu — no asking, just decide.
Show the last thing you searched on your phone. No skipping.
Give each other a nickname right now. It has to stick for the rest of the night.
Swap seats and answer the next card as if you were them.
Write a one-line review of this date so far. Read it out loud.
Raise a toast to how you ended up here tonight.
Show the name of the group chat you talk in most.
Draw each other from memory in under thirty seconds. No peeking.
Hand over your phone. They read your last three notifications, no explaining.
Slow dance for ten seconds. No music needed.
Say the nickname your friends would give this date if they were watching.
Take one selfie together. No retakes, no filters.
Whisper your answer to the next card instead of saying it out loud.
Trade phones for one minute and change each other's contact name to something honest.
Set a one-minute timer and take turns naming everything you find attractive about the other person — no repeats, no stopping early.
Swap a piece of jewelry or an accessory and wear it for the rest of the night.
Act out how you'd introduce each other to your best friend, right now, in character.
final: Before you leave each other tonight, open your notes.
Write down one thing you want them to know — the thing you'd regret not saying.
Don't read it out. Send it once you're home.
